questions.question: The main cause of periodicity in the properties of elements is the
options: repetition of similar outermost electronic configurations at certain intervals
increase in the number of neutrons
questions.explanation: Periodicity arises because elements with similar outermost electronic configurations recur at regular intervals, giving similar chemical properties.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a periodic property?
questions.explanation: Atomic number increases monotonically and is not a periodic property. Atomic radius, ionization energy, and electronegativity vary periodically.

questions.question: Elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have similar chemical properties because they have the same
questions.explanation: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons, which determines their chemical behaviour.

questions.question: Going from left to right across a period, the number of electron shells
questions.explanation: Across a period, electrons are added to the same shell, so the number of shells remains the same.

questions.question: Going down a group, the number of electron shells
questions.explanation: Going down a group, a new shell is added for each period, so the number of electron shells increases.

questions.question: An element with electronic configuration 2, 8, 1 belongs to group
questions.explanation: The outermost shell has 1 electron, so the element belongs to Group I.

questions.question: An element with electronic configuration 2, 8, 7 is in period
questions.explanation: There are 3 occupied shells (2, 8, 7), so the element is in Period 3.

questions.question: Which sub-atomic particle has a negligible mass compared with the others?
questions.explanation: The electron has a mass about 1/1836 that of a proton, so it is negligible compared with protons and neutrons.

questions.question: The sub-atomic particle that carries no charge is the
questions.explanation: The neutron is electrically neutral (no charge).

questions.question: The nucleus of an atom contains
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons; electrons occupy the shells around it.

questions.question: Atomic radius is the distance between
options: the nuclei of two different atoms
the centre of the nucleus and the outermost electron shell of an atom
the first and the last electron shells
the protons and neutrons in the nucleus
questions.explanation: Atomic radius is the distance from the centre of the nucleus to the outermost electron shell.

questions.question: Atomic radius is the same as
questions.explanation: Atomic radius is a measure of atomic size.

questions.question: In a diatomic molecule such as H<sub>2</sub>, the atomic radius is taken as
options: twice the distance between the two nuclei
half the distance between the two nuclei
equal to the distance between the two nuclei
one-quarter of the distance between the two nuclei
questions.explanation: For a diatomic molecule, the atomic radius is half the internuclear distance.

questions.question: Down a group in the Periodic Table, atomic radius
questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group because new shells are added.

questions.question: The trend in atomic radius down a group is mainly due to
options: an increase in the number of electron shells
an increase in the number of neutrons
a decrease in the number of valence electrons
questions.explanation: Down a group, the number of electron shells increases, so the outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus.

questions.question: In potassium (2, 8, 8, 1), the outermost electron is in the
questions.explanation: The fourth shell is the N shell, so the outermost electron is in the N shell.

questions.question: Across a period from left to right, atomic radius generally
questions.explanation: Across a period, increasing nuclear charge pulls the same shell closer, so atomic radius decreases.

questions.question: The trend in atomic radius across a period is due to
options: increasing nuclear charge attracting electrons in the same shell more strongly
questions.explanation: Across a period, increasing nuclear charge attracts the same-shell electrons more strongly, shrinking the radius.

questions.question: Which of the following has the largest atomic radius?
questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases down Group I, so Cs has the largest radius.

questions.question: Which of the following period 3 elements has the smallest atomic radius?
questions.explanation: Across Period 3, radius decreases from left to right, so Cl has the smallest radius.

questions.question: Which of chlorine and bromine has the larger atomic radius, and why?
options: Chlorine, because it has more electrons
They are equal because they are in the same group
Bromine, because it has more electron shells
Chlorine, because it has higher electronegativity
questions.explanation: Bromine is below chlorine in Group VII and has more electron shells, so it has the larger atomic radius.

questions.question: Which arrangement shows decreasing atomic radius?
questions.explanation: Across Period 3, radius decreases from left to right, so Na > Mg > Al > Si is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following period 2 elements (excluding the noble gas) has the largest atomic radius?
questions.explanation: Across Period 2, radius decreases from left to right, so Li has the largest radius.

questions.question: Which arrangement shows increasing atomic radius?
questions.explanation: Across Period 2, radius decreases from left to right, so increasing order is F < O < N < C.

questions.question: A cation has a radius that is ______ the radius of its parent atom.
questions.explanation: A cation loses its outermost shell, so its radius is smaller than that of the parent atom.

questions.question: The radius of a cation is smaller than that of its parent atom because
options: the outermost shell is lost and the nucleus pulls the remaining electrons more strongly
questions.explanation: When the outermost shell is lost, the remaining electrons are pulled more strongly by the same nuclear charge, so the cation is smaller.

questions.question: An anion has a radius that is ______ the radius of its parent atom.
questions.explanation: An anion gains extra electrons, increasing repulsion, so its radius is larger than that of the parent atom.

questions.question: The radius of an anion is larger than that of its parent atom because
options: protons are lost from the nucleus
the extra electrons increase repulsion and are less strongly attracted by the nucleus
questions.explanation: The extra electrons increase repulsion and are less strongly attracted, so the anion expands.

questions.question: Which is larger, Na or Na<sup>+</sup>?
questions.explanation: The neutral atom Na is larger than Na+, which has lost its outermost shell.

questions.question: Which is larger, Cl or Cl<sup>−</sup>?
questions.explanation: Cl− is larger than Cl because the extra electron increases repulsion.

questions.question: Which of the following isoelectronic ions has the smallest radius?
questions.explanation: For isoelectronic ions, higher nuclear charge gives smaller radius, so Mg2+ is smallest.

questions.question: Which of the following isoelectronic ions has the largest radius?
questions.explanation: For isoelectronic ions, lower nuclear charge gives larger radius, so O2− is largest.

questions.question: Down a group, the ionic radius of ions with the same charge
questions.explanation: Ionic radius increases down a group as more shells are added.

questions.question: K<sup>+</sup> and Ca<sup>2+</sup> have the same electronic configuration (2, 8, 8). Which is larger, and why?
options: K<sup>+</sup>, because it has fewer protons
Ca<sup>2+</sup>, because it has more protons
Ca<sup>2+</sup>, because it has more electrons
questions.explanation: For isoelectronic ions, K+ has fewer protons (lower nuclear charge), so it is larger than Ca2+.

questions.question: Ionization energy is the energy required to
options: add an electron to a gaseous atom
remove a valence electron from an atom to form an ion
attract a shared pair of electrons in a bond
questions.explanation: Ionization energy is the energy needed to remove a valence electron from a gaseous atom.

questions.question: A high ionization energy for an atom means that
options: its electron is difficult to remove
questions.explanation: High ionization energy means the electron is difficult to remove.

questions.question: Down a group, the ionization energy
questions.explanation: Ionization energy decreases down a group as the outermost electron is farther from the nucleus.

questions.question: Ionization energy decreases down a group because the outermost electron is
options: farther from the nucleus and less strongly held
attracted by a larger number of valence electrons
questions.explanation: The outermost electron is farther from the nucleus and more shielded, so it is less strongly held.

questions.question: Across a period from left to right, the ionization energy generally
questions.explanation: Ionization energy generally increases across a period as nuclear charge increases.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest first ionization energy?
questions.explanation: Ar has a stable noble-gas configuration, so it has the highest first ionization energy among the listed elements.

questions.question: Which of the following loses its valence electron most easily?
questions.explanation: Ionization energy decreases down Group I, so Cs loses its valence electron most easily.

questions.question: The usual unit of ionization energy is
questions.explanation: Ionization energy is usually expressed in kJ mol−1.

questions.question: The second ionization energy of an element is greater than its first because
options: the ion has more shells than the atom
an electron is being removed from a positively charged ion
the atom is larger than the ion
questions.explanation: The second electron is removed from a positively charged ion, so more energy is required.

questions.question: Electron affinity is the energy change that occurs when
options: a gaseous atom gains an electron to form a negative ion
an electron is removed from an atom
an atom attracts a shared pair of electrons
an atom loses a valence electron
questions.explanation: Electron affinity is the energy change when a gaseous atom gains an electron.

questions.question: Atoms with smaller atomic radii tend to have
questions.explanation: Smaller atoms hold their electrons closer, so they have a stronger attraction for electrons.

questions.question: Down a group, electron affinity generally
questions.explanation: Electron affinity generally decreases down a group as atomic size increases.

questions.question: Across a period from left to right, electron affinity generally
questions.explanation: Electron affinity generally increases across a period as atoms become smaller and more electron-attracting.

questions.question: Noble gases have no tendency to accept additional electrons because
options: their outermost shells are already complete
they have only one valence electron
questions.explanation: Noble gases have complete outermost shells, so they do not accept additional electrons.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest electron affinity?
questions.explanation: Cl has a high electron affinity, greater than Na, Mg, and P.

questions.question: Electronegativity is the ability of an atom to
options: attract shared pairs of electrons to itself in a chemical bond
remove an electron from another atom
release energy when it gains an electron
questions.explanation: Electronegativity is the ability to attract shared pairs of electrons in a bond.

questions.question: The most electronegative element is
questions.explanation: Fluorine (F) is the most electronegative element.

questions.question: Down a group, electronegativity
questions.explanation: Electronegativity decreases down a group as atomic size increases.

questions.question: Across a period from left to right, electronegativity
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period as nuclear charge increases.

questions.question: Metals are generally characterised by
questions.explanation: Metals have low electronegativity; they tend to lose electrons rather than attract them.

questions.question: Which arrangement shows increasing electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period, so the correct increasing order is Na < Mg < Al < Cl.

questions.question: Electropositivity is the
options: tendency of an atom to attract electrons
tendency of an atom to lose electrons to form a positive ion
energy released when an atom gains an electron
ability of an atom to conduct electricity
questions.explanation: Electropositivity is the tendency to lose electrons and form positive ions.

questions.question: In general, electropositivity
options: decreases down a group and increases across a period
increases down a group and decreases across a period
increases both down a group and across a period
decreases both down a group and across a period
questions.explanation: Electropositivity increases down a group and decreases across a period.

questions.question: Which of the following Group II elements is the most electropositive?
questions.explanation: Electropositivity increases down Group II, so Ba is the most electropositive.

questions.question: Metals are generally
options: poor conductors of heat and electricity
good conductors of heat and electricity
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity.

questions.question: Within a period, the melting and boiling points of metallic elements generally
questions.explanation: Within a period, the melting and boiling points of metallic elements generally increase from left to right as metallic bonding strengthens.
